enhancement_evidence.claim: A per-citation contest-worthiness score from historical outcomes can be delivered inside the 10-day conference window using public MSHA and FMSHRC data (dossier mind-changer: issuance-to-public-file lag under 5 days)
enhancement_evidence.support: Partially supported, with a reframe that survives the adversarial attack. Cadence receipt: MDRS/open-data files are republished every Friday, so publish lag alone runs 0-7 days from MSHA data entry; a measured sub-5-day issuance-to-appearance lag is NOT publicly documented and must be measured empirically by diffing weekly violations files against their citation issue-date fields (feasible, since issue dates are in the record layout). The latency risk only affects auto-detection of brand-new citations: under 30 CFR 100.6 the 10-day clock starts upon MSHA notice to the operator, who already holds the paper citation, so the packet can be triggered by operator upload of the citation while the value layer, historical comparables from the violations back-file plus published FMSHRC decisions and the joint DOL/MSHA/FMSHRC backlog data (about 9,200 new contest cases filed in FY2009, 14,200 pending, 209M USD in contested fines), is latency-insensitive. Commercial precedent that outcome-and-penalty modeling on this exact data sells: Newmont's 3-year Predictive Compliance subscription, and MSHAWISE marketing an AI case-law copilot specifically for informal conference prep.
